:rotating_light: _new alert — needs human_
Channel: `alert-system`  -  confidence: 0.60  -  bug-type guess: `env`  -  alerts in group: 2

*Symptoms:*
• DD monitor *"RTC Screen Load has a high p95 latency"* (ID 115456700) fired at 2026-05-06 *06*:03:*20 UTC*, triggered by `POST /api/v1/runtime/load/_screenid*` p95 exceeding 3s threshold
• Resolved within minutes (monitor now OK)
• Concurrent frontend errors in `method-ui` at 06:01–06:05 UTC:
    ◦ Multiple `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` (heavy layout, downstream of slow loads)
    ◦ *XHR errors on sync-widget API* across 3+ accounts: `cbma`, `foreigntaxcpa`, `deccanfoods4` — all hitting `GET /gateway/syncutil/syncwidget/{account}/GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync?viewNameFriendly=Estimate`
    ◦ `AngularJS PlatformCtrl is not a function, got undefined` (legacy UI controller load failure)
    ◦ `Minified Redux error #7` (store mismatch following failed API responses)
• p95 screen load was elevated in window: 2.697s at 05:55, ~3s+ at 06:02–06:03, 2.383s at 06:05
• *All-time peak this window: 3.457s yesterday (2026-05-05 14:45 UTC)*
*Trace IDs:* not captured (no matching log-level errors from `runtime-core-api` itself during window — spike is at latency level only)

*Likely cause:* Transient latency spike on `runtime-core-api` screen load path — consistent with a short GC pause or memory pressure event on the IIS/Kestrel process. Cascading XHR failures to sync-widget are a downstream symptom (users with Estimate screen open polling sync status, timing out during the slow window).

*Recurring pattern:*
• `runtime-core-api` error rate monitor also fired *2026-05-04* (last_triggered 2026-05-04T18:52:15Z)
• `runtime-core-api` p90 latency also fired *2026-05-04* (last_triggered 2026-05-04T18:52:45Z)
• This is the 3rd latency event in 3 days
*Suggested next action:* Check IIS app pool memory/GC counters for `runtime-core` around 06:02–06:03 UTC and during the May 4 event. If memory is climbing between recycles, there may be a leak. Also consider correlating with screen ID — if the same customer's heavy screen is causing p95 outliers, the trace would reveal it. `ms-sync-util`/sync-widget errors may self-resolve but worth confirming.

:rotating_light: _new alert — needs human_
Channel: `alert-frontend-errors`  -  confidence: 0.55  -  bug-type guess: `env`  -  alerts in group: 3

*Symptoms:*
• `GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync` XHR failing with HTTP status 0 ("Failed to load") — network-level, no HTTP response received
• 7 accounts affected: `back2internationalltd` (6 errors), `holdit` (3), `bramattcomputingltd` (3), `dentmagicswltd` (2), `antaressaddle` (3, but these are `n.clarity.ms` — 3rd-party, benign), `changeit` (1), `symbiosisuklimited` (1)
• Datadog monitor _"Unusual number of XHR errors for account"_ fired 3× between 08:09–08:16 UTC, then returned to OK
• Individual errors still occurring as of 09:08 UTC (users opening Estimates/Invoices continue to see widget failures)
• Gateway route `GET /syncutil/syncwidget/{account}/GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync` → `microservices.methodlocal.int:80` is correctly configured in `ocelot.syncutil.json`; the issue is downstream of the gateway
*Trace IDs / Request IDs:* `AwAAAZ38i_06Ybp8` (back2internationalltd, 09:08 UTC), `AwAAAZ33azp0fVxC` (dentmagicswltd, baseline)

*Likely cause:* Transient unavailability of the `ms-sync-util` virtual app on `microservices.methodlocal.int`. HTTP status 0 = connection refused / connection reset at the IIS level — the gateway can't reach the downstream host. Consistent with an IIS pool recycle or the `microservices` pool being briefly overwhelmed. The spike at 08:09–08:16 UTC aligns with no recent deploys to `ms-sync-util` (last commit >3 days ago), so pool recycle is the top hypothesis.

*Suggested next action:* Check `microservices.methodlocal.int` IIS event log for pool recycle events around 08:09 UTC. If the pool recycled automatically (memory/crash), check `ms-sync-util` application logs for unhandled exceptions. If still failing: recycle the `microservices` IIS pool manually to get a clean state, then monitor for 5 min.

:rotating_light: _new alert — needs human_
Channel: alert-runtime-monitoring  -  confidence: 0.68  -  bug-type guess: code/deploy  -  alerts in group: 2

*Symptoms:*
• `POST /api/v1/runtime/load/_screenid` p95 *max 23.274s* in last hour (monitor threshold: 3s)
• `POST /api/v1/grid/_screenid` p95 *max 11.949s*
• `POST /api/v1/runtime/_actionid_` p95 *max 5.336s*
• Monitor 115456700 "RTC Screen Load has a high p95 latency" fired at 06:03 UTC today (now OK, intermittent)
• Request rate and error rate are within normal baseline (avg ~9 req/s, no tracked errors)
• Two near-simultaneous alerts (10:13:49 and 10:13:51 UTC) — likely screen-load + action-execution monitors firing together
*Likely cause:* Commit `23cfed4` (deployed ~2026-05-05 18:37 UTC, branch `claude/confident-babbage-cOtZN`) made two changes to `runtime-core`:
1. `appsettings.prod.json`: `MaxUserBundlePairs` *30 → 50* — allows up to 50 bundle pairs per request (was 30), increasing per-request data load on screen loads
2. `Apps/Apps.Api/Attributes/EnforceBundleLimitAttribute.cs`: *removed `X-Bypass-Bundle-Limit: true` header* bypass — internal service calls that previously skipped the limit check now go through full bundle validation on every request
Both changes together may cause slow screen loads for accounts with many installed apps, and add overhead to every request now that the bypass is gone.

*Suggested next action:*
• Check if reverting `MaxUserBundlePairs` prod *50 → 30* resolves screen load latency (1-line config rollback in `appsettings.prod.json`)
• OR investigate which accounts have high bundle counts (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM BundlePairs GROUP BY AccountId ORDER BY 2 DESC`) to confirm only a subset of tenants are affected
• Decide whether to restore the bypass header for internal service calls in `EnforceBundleLimitAttribute.cs`

:rotating_light: _new alert — needs human_
Channel: alert-frontend-errors  -  confidence: 0.52  -  bug-type guess: env (syncwidget) + code (Redux)  -  alerts in group: 1

*Note:* Alert message content was not surfaced by the Slack MCP (likely attachment-only payload from bot B011R3D650X). Investigation based on DD browser error logs around the alert time.

*Symptoms (last 2h, service:method-ui, env:production):*
• `XHR error GET /gateway/syncutil/syncwidget/{account}/GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync` — *8 occurrences, status:0 (network fail)*, multiple accounts: marylanddecking3, shasep, prostack, plus others. This is a persistent pattern, not one-off.
• `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '@@redux-saga/SAGA_ACTION')` — account `hilltimespublishinginc`, Portal app, same session, redux-saga dispatcher receiving undefined action. Accompanied by 3× `Minified Redux error #7`.
• `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'o.id')` — account `refexpertsandhvacllc`, Safari, 3× same session.
• `turfprepsales.method.me` — cluster of 4 different API failures in same window (apps/screen, enqueuejobs, runtime, preferences) — suggests a transient per-account connectivity event, not a new bug.
• `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` — 20× total, benign browser noise (no-op).
• `XHR error POST clarity.ms` — 7×, Microsoft Clarity analytics; third-party network, not Method infra.
*Prod frontend version:* `master.2026-05-01_14:32:28z` — the May 5 UI commits (PL-61861 email API migration, ManagePermissions fix) are *not yet deployed to prod*.

*Most actionable finding — syncwidget failures:*
`/gateway/syncutil/syncwidget/{account}/GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync` is failing at the network level (HTTP status 0) across multiple unrelated accounts. This endpoint goes through ms-gateway-api → syncutil (likely `legacy-syncservice-api`). Check:
1. Is `legacy-syncservice-api` running and healthy? (`/health/check` on IIS `legacy` pool)
2. Are there IIS pool recycles affecting the sync endpoint around 10:13–11:02 UTC?
3. Is this a new pattern or chronic noise? (if chronic, add to false-alarms.json)
*Suggested next action:* Check `legacy-syncservice-api` health via IIS; if it shows recycles, investigate `legacy` pool stability. File a defect for the `hilltimespublishinginc` redux-saga crash separately.

*Symptoms:*
• 6 alerts from bot B063S8NBW0M in 3 tight pairs at 11:15, 11:41, and 11:45 UTC (alert text unreadable — Block Kit messages not surfaced by MCP)
• RTC Screen Load p95 latency hit 2.24–2.38s at 11:23, 11:31, 11:32 UTC (threshold for alert is 3s; monitor 115456700 is in *Warn* state and fired earlier today at 06:03 UTC — possible warning sub-threshold)
• runtime-core-api throughput during alert window averaged 15.48 req/s vs weekly Wednesday baseline of 22.42 req/s (~31% below)
• Single throughput dip to 8.45 req/s at 11:43 UTC (yesterday same-hour min was 9.40)
• ms-account-api dependency monitors (redis, sql-server, mongodb) have been in *No Data* since 2026-05-02 (~4 days) — ms-account-api itself is healthy at 13.97 req/s avg
• Zero error-rate hits across all services for the past hour

*Trace IDs:* none recoverable (DD logs returned empty for window; ES unavailable)

*Likely cause:* Monitor 115456700 (RTC Screen Load p95) crossing a warning sub-threshold (~2.0s?) during brief latency spikes — 3 firings in 31 min consistent with a 10–15 min alert window re-evaluating. Root cause of the latency spikes is unclear. Possible contributing factors: (a) the sustained No Data state on ms-account-api's redis/sql/mongo dependencies since 2026-05-02 (infra reconfiguration?); (b) traffic running 31% below weekly baseline (lower concurrency → cold caches?).

*Suggested next actions:*
1. Open the RTC Screen Load monitor (115456700) in Datadog and review the warning threshold — if it's set at 2.0s and spikes are transient, consider whether the threshold needs tuning or adding to false-alarms KB
2. Investigate why ms-account-api dependency monitors (redis: 65577145/65577146, sql-server: 65603306/65603311, mongodb: 65603337/65603338) went No Data on 2026-05-02 — were these dependencies decommissioned/reconfigured?

*Symptoms:*
• 6 Centreon Monitoring alerts (B03GBAMHUTB), 08:54:36–09:00:58 EDT
• Centreon monitors infrastructure components (IIS pools, RabbitMQ, Redis, network). Message text not recoverable (attachment-only payload)

• DD monitor 70171778 ("Unexpected number of 5XX errors") fired at 13:11 UTC — confirms >30 5XX in 5 min
*Trace IDs:* not recoverable (gateway APM logs not indexed in DD; ES unavailable 403)

*Likely cause:* Transient downstream service instability causing gateway to return 5XX. Leading suspects: `ms-documents-api` (.NET 10 upgrade deployed 2026-05-05 14:07 EDT, PL-61881) and `ms-email-api` (v1→v2 route migration re-applied 2026-05-05 14:28 EDT, PL-61861). Gateway itself received new v2 document routes in the same deploy window. No other service (runtime-core-api, authentication, etc.) shows errors during this period.

*Suggested next action:* Check `ms-documents-api` logs and IIS pool health for 08:54–09:07 EDT. Verify the new `.NET 10` document endpoints are responding correctly. If any pool crashed-and-recycled, that would explain the two bursts. Also confirm whether Centreon alerts are for an IIS pool recycle or network check.
